I am 54 years old, and I have been farming these 8 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. I only finished primary school, so I do not read books about farming — I watch what my neighbors do, I listen to the seed dealer, and I remember what worked last year. I split my land into two parts: 5 mu in wheat-maize rotation because that brings steady money, and 3 mu in cotton because cotton prices were decent last year and my family can pick it ourselves.

For wheat, I plant an improved variety in October. Last year I used 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as base, and top-dressed with 40 jin of urea in spring. The yield was good — almost 500 jin per mu. This year fertilizer prices are still high, but I would rather spend more than risk a bad harvest. I will use the same: 80 jin of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer and 40 jin of urea. That is about 15 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate three times — before winter, at jointing, and when the grain is filling. I spray twice for aphids and powdery mildew. I rotary till before planting. I expect 500 kg per mu.

For maize on the same 5 mu after wheat harvest, I plant a hybrid variety right away — there is no time to waste in June. I do not deep plow; I plant directly into the wheat stubble to save time and keep moisture. I put 70 jin of compound fertilizer per mu and side-dress with 30 jin of urea when the plants are knee-high. That is about 12 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice if the rain does not come — once after planting if it is dry, and once at tasseling. I spray herbicide once and insecticide once if I see armyworms. I expect 580 kg per mu.

For cotton on my 3 mu, I plant a hybrid in April. Cotton needs more pesticide because of bollworms, so I spray three times. I put down 80 jin of compound fertilizer and 20 jin of urea, which is about 11 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice — once at flowering and once at boll stage. I rotary till before planting. Expected yield is around 280 kg of seed cotton per mu. I watch my neighbors closely, and if everyone around me applies a certain amount, I do something similar. Change is risky, and a bad harvest is a disaster.
